body:
A Taiwan crisis may start with paperwork, not missiles: a coast guard "quarantine" that CSIS says "is not a declaration of war." The first seven days, built from published war games.

New video:
youtu.be/FpXvEcxnLj0

No deal in Brussels. After almost 14 hours, EU leaders left without agreeing on a EUR 45bn (about $49bn) loan to fund Ukraine in 2027, or on the long-term budget.

Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia say they won't join a joint loan. Both files go to the December summit (AP, bne IntelliNews).

Two Rheinmetall Italia technicians died Thursday at a Kuwaiti air-defense site, hit by shrapnel from intercepted drones, Kuwait says. They were servicing Skyguard detection antennas. Kuwait blames Iran; Tehran denies it (Arab News, Arab Times).
The oil that left Hormuz didn't vanish. A lot of it moved west. Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea's southern gate, went from 5.4 to 8.1 million barrels a day (EIA). That makes it the gate that matters now.

The State Department cleared a possible $621.9M F-16 sustainment sale to Ukraine on 25 Nov: parts, lab equipment, transport support.

Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway are paying. No US funds, State says. Earlier packages were $266.4M and $310.5M. (Photo: file, 2011)
Bases get 90 days. Families get 3. That's the gap in this fall's Western preparedness plans.

Ukraine's General Staff says it hit three MiG-31s and two Su-34s at Savasleyka airbase in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region. Figures are preliminary and Moscow hasn't commented (Al Jazeera, Kyiv Post). Card photo: file.

Hormuz oil flows: 21.6 million barrels a day before the war, 4.9 million by spring (EIA). The way around it, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, is now a target by Houthi claims, and the Red Sea's southern gate is wobbling.

New video:
youtu.be/nIvqdESKYiE

Putin told oil executives on 24 Nov that retaliation for Ukraine's refinery strikes is "inevitable" and called Russia's fuel situation "challenging."

Andrii Sybiha's reply on X: "Stop complaining."

Several Russian regions now cap retail fuel sales. (Reuters, CNBC)
Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz while under US escort. Unverified: reports differ on two tankers or three, and CENTCOM hadn't commented as of Tuesday.

Sweden mailed a crisis booklet to every household. Germany says up to 10 days of supplies, Britain 3, the EU 72 hours.

The long US plan is for military bases: 90 days on their own, per internal Pentagon documents reported by Fox News Digital.
Kyiv says its drones hit Lukoil's refinery in Perm on 23 Nov, about 930 miles (1,500 km) from Ukraine. Perm's regional officials report damage at an unnamed industrial site.

In Moscow's words. Putin to reporters, 2 Dec 2025, in Russian: "Мы не собираемся воевать с Европой, я уже об этом сто раз сказал. Но если Европа вдруг захочет воевать и начнёт, мы готовы прямо сейчас."
Word for word: "We are not going to fight Europe, I have already said this a hundred times. But if Europe suddenly wants to fight and starts, we are ready right now."
Danish military intelligence, Feb 2025: Russia "perceives itself as being in conflict with the West and is preparing for a war against NATO."
Which of those two you believe shapes how you read every Kremlin statement. The full NATO scenario: youtu.be/4Yg1JGsH5Xo

US diesel hit $6.52 a gallon on 22 September, the highest ever recorded. Reuters pinned it on two things: the war with Iran and Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries. Worth remembering next time someone says a war far away doesn't touch you.

NATO's civil resilience requirements are public for the first time. US bases are told to plan for 90 days without the grid (internal documents, per Fox News Digital). Families: 3 to 10 days.

New video on what they're preparing for:

youtu.be/rsqPreXS7qc

Zelensky, 22 Nov: "it is particularly difficult to understand the delays in the delivery of anti-ballistic systems to Ukraine."

Allies paid for Patriots via NATO's PURL fund. Moving US-made missiles from third countries needs Washington's OK. (Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform)

Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery, about 100 miles (165 km) north of Jeddah on the Red Sea coast. They say it was a direct hit.

No damage confirmed. Saudi authorities hadn't commented, per Reuters and CNBC (22-23 Nov).

Russia's refineries are running about 45% below late-October levels after Ukraine's drone campaign, two industry sources told Reuters on 18 Nov.

15 of 35 major plants disrupted or halted, up from 9 a week before. Gasoline rationing is already back in some regions.

Zelensky on the Article 5-style offer, 21 Nov: "So far, I have not seen such commitments on paper."

His questions: who's in the collective, how it would defend Ukraine, and whether it would really repel an attack. He wants it for decades, not two years. (Kyiv Independent)

Three pivot points from this week: a bridge in the sea, a summit with no deal, and a strait getting worse.

(File photos: Kyiv's Podil bridge, 2019; Putin and Xi, 2025; Iranian forces board a tanker, 2020)

Driving for Thanksgiving? AAA had gas at $3.81 a gallon on 16 Nov, up from $3.07 a year ago. The holiday record is $3.58 (2022); if prices hold, it falls this week.

Flying won't save you: AAA says round trips average $800, up 17%.

Putin on war with Europe, in his own words: "we are ready right now."

The Russian original, a word-for-word translation, then the check against Danish military intelligence. Defensive warning or a threat?

$3.54 to $5.02 a gallon in under four months. That's what the last war in Europe did to US gas (AAA), and America wasn't even fighting.

What would a wider war do this time?

Every conflict has a pivot point.

Wars, and what they cost you. Every claim sourced, every map checked. New full videos Mon, Wed and Fri on YouTube.

youtube.com/@Fulcrum...

Music: humanoide9000, CC BY 4.0. Footage: DVIDS, NATO, Ukraine's border guard (CC BY 4.0), Pixabay.

"Ukraine hit 30% of Russia's refineries." Not quite.

Reuters: 9 of 35 major refineries disrupted in one week, about 30% of capacity by plant size. Actual fuel loss, per Reuters' sources: up to 200,000 of ~700,000 tons a day.

The danger for Taiwan right now isn't an attack. It's a lesson.

Beijing is learning how far a Middle East war can pull America away from Asia. A carrier can sail back in weeks. A lesson like that stays.

Hormuz: attacks on shipping are at their highest level of the war (ABC News, maritime data). UKMTO put traffic ~65% below pre-war in mid-November.

An Iranian lawmaker says Chinese ships get through (SCMP).

(File photo, 2020)

Day 3 of a war game run by Die Welt and Germany's military university: Russia holds Marijampolė in Lithuania.

Washington didn't trigger Article 5. Germany hesitated. Poland stopped at a mined border. A game, not a forecast.

Every war has a pivot point: the moment the balance of power moves.

We find it, map it and source it, then show what it costs you. New breakdowns Mon, Wed and Fri on YouTube.

youtube.com/@Fulcrum...

Music: humanoide9000, CC BY 4.0. Footage: DVIDS, NATO, Ukraine's border guard (CC BY 4.0), Pixabay.

Nine refineries in one week. Rationing at the pump. A budget deficit heading for nearly double the plan.

New video: Ukraine Is Setting Russia's War Money on Fire. And why it's still not a collapse.

youtu.be/R-xiFPGLiQs

Shenzhen produced a photo, not a deal. The first Trump-Xi-Putin meeting ran about 90 minutes (CBS) and ended with a short joint statement.

(File photo: Putin and Xi, 2025)

Three days. That's how long Russia needed to take a NATO city in a December 2025 war game. Washington never triggered Article 5.

How it played out, and why Baltic critics hate it:

Shenzhen today: the first meeting ever of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders together.

Trump opened on nuclear arms. The three are "uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on earth," he said.

(File photo: Trump and Putin, Alaska 2025)
Xi, per Chinese state media, called for nuclear weapons to be banned and destroyed outright. Putin wanted energy security and the war in Ukraine on the table.

No agreement had been announced as of the opening remarks. What to watch: anything concrete on Ukraine, and whether arms talks get a format and a date.

CNBC: cnbc.com/2026/11/19/...

None of the published NATO war games start with tanks.

A leaked German scenario (via Euronews, Jan 2024) opens with cyberattacks and a story about mistreated Russian speakers. The troops move later, next to the Suwalki Gap.

Russian forces at the edge of two NATO capitals in 60 hours. That's what RAND's war games found.

New video, the first 72 hours day by day. A scenario, not a prediction.

youtu.be/4Yg1JGsH5Xo
Trump heads to Shenzhen for APEC this week. On the latest USNI fleet tracker (16 Nov), zero of the US Navy's 11 carriers were deployed near China.
Third time since Friday. Iran's IRGC says its drones went for a US radar at Isa air base in Bahrain today. Air defenses knocked them down. The US says no damage, nobody hurt (Al Jazeera).
